## Purpose and provenance

The block-eigen operator is a summary-statistics LD representation constructed
from selected PLINK BED reference genotypes. Public ST and MT fitters require
the BED source, selected samples and markers, block starts, allele frequencies,
and summary-statistic provenance needed to prove marker and scale alignment.
Current MT use requires summary statistics derived from the same selected BED
genotypes by construction; arbitrary external GWAS projection is not supported.

“Block eigen” describes how within-block LD is constructed and filtered. The
runtime sampler uses reconstructed dense filtered blocks, stored as packed
upper triangles, rather than necessarily retaining low-rank eigenfactors.

## Construction

Markers and samples are resolved once from `Glist`, `rows`, and selected BED
columns. BED genotypes are decoded, missing values are replaced according to
the aligned allele-frequency/standardization contract, and columns are put on
the standardized-genotype scale. `block_start` is one-based at the public R
boundary; blocks must be positive, contiguous, non-overlapping, and cover the
complete selected marker order.

For each block, the implementation forms the standardized within-block
cross-product/correlation representation, symmetrizes it, and computes its
eigendecomposition. The chosen filter changes the represented operator:

- `hard_truncate`: eigenvalues below the nonnegative `eigen_tau` threshold are
  removed, and the summary score `wy` is projected consistently into the
  retained eigenspace;
- `ridge_fixed`: a fixed nonnegative `eigen_eta` ridge/shrinkage policy is
  applied while `wy` remains on its original aligned score scale;
- `ridge_lw`: a Ledoit–Wolf-style block shrinkage estimate is used, with the
  implementation's positive floor and block diagnostics; `wy` is not hard
  projected.

Filtering parameters and block diagnostics are retained in fit metadata.

## Diagonal meanings

Three diagonals must not be conflated:

- input `ww`: the supplied summary-statistic marker information;
- unfiltered reference diagonal: the diagonal before spectral filtering;
- filtered runtime diagonal: the diagonal of the reconstructed operator
  actually used by marker updates and by `vle`.

The block-eigen summary route validates input `ww` as provenance but does not
substitute it for the filtered runtime diagonal. The runtime diagonal is
positive and exactly matches the diagonal stored in each packed block.

## Runtime representation and ownership

Each reconstructed symmetric block stores only its upper triangle in
single-precision packed order plus marker-to-block/local-index mappings and a
double-precision diagonal view. Immutable storage is prepared once per fit and
borrowed by logical chains. Worker tasks own sampler state but do not rebuild
or copy the operator.

A marker update visits its within-block off-diagonal entries, so the update
cost is proportional to its block size. Storage is

\[
O\!\left(\sum_b m_b(m_b+1)/2\right),
\]

not (O(mr)) low-rank storage. Narrower blocks lower memory and update cost but
set cross-block LD to zero.

## Public support

- `stblr_block_eigen()`: `sbayesc`, `sbayesr`, `sbayesrc`;
- `mtblr_block_eigen()`: `sbayesc`, `sbayesr`, `sbayesrc`.

The `sbayesrc` ST route uses its public `annotation` input; the MT route uses
`annotations`. Fixed `selection_s` requires aligned allele frequencies and
explicit provenance. Exact unfiltered construction is used in permanent
reductions against CSR when both represent the same LD operator.

## Practical limitations

- Cross-block LD is not represented.
- Filtering changes the likelihood operator and must be reported.
- External-GWAS/reference-LD use requires a scale/projection contract not
  supplied by the current block-eigen API.
- Runtime storage may be dense within blocks even after eigen filtering.
- Reference samples, marker order, allele orientation, missing-value policy,
  frequencies, block boundaries, and filter settings are required provenance.

See [Data representations](../notes/data_representations.qmd) and the
[operator comparison workflow](https://github.com/psoerensen/sblr/blob/master/examples/workflows/operator_comparison_workflow.R).
